name: RoboChem-Flex: low-cost 3D-printed self-driving lab for reaction optimisation (Noël group, 2026)
brief: A flow self-driving lab for optimising organic reaction conditions at 5-50 micromole scale: syringe pumps dose reagents into a flow reactor and a liquid sampling unit on a Cartesian robot collects reaction aliquots, which are analysed offline on a shared analytical instrument (human-in-the-loop).

cost.original: approximately US$5,000 (human-in-the-loop configuration with 3D-printed liquid sampling unit, excluding analytical equipment)
cost.excludes_note: Excludes analytical instruments (assumed available in a shared facility) and the inline-analytics configuration; assembly labour not stated. The authors call it approximate.

notes: Verified 3 Oct 2026 against the primary paper (Pilon et al., Nat. Synth. 2026, DOI 10.1038/s44160-026-01053-0): "reducing the overall system cost to approximately US$5,000". Supplementary BOM not yet read; no throughput in the main text, so reported.throughput is left empty. Chemistry World page could not be read in full.
